name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about 19 points Republican and Thompson is a long-serving incumbent
Thompson has roughly a 13-to-1 fundraising edge over Bilger
Prediction markets price a Republican win at about 95 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; challenger has minimal campaign infrastructure
model.rationale: Glenn Thompson combines a roughly 19-point Republican district lean with a large fundraising advantage and no meaningful outside spending against him, while markets give him about a 95 percent win probability. Even a favorable national environment for Democrats leaves Ray Bilger with too little money and visibility to close a gap this wide.
model.watch: A major late surge in national Democratic spending or an unusually strong Democratic wave year could narrow the margin, though it is unlikely to put the seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
PA-15 is a heavily Republican district in north-central Pennsylvania, and Glenn Thompson has held the seat since 2009. He is seeking another term with a large financial edge, having raised about $1.85 million and holding roughly $830,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Ray Bilger has raised about $140,000 with minimal cash. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race, and no public general-election polls have been conducted.

Prediction markets give Thompson roughly a 95 percent chance of winning, and the district's partisan lean of about 19 points Republican leaves little room for an upset. Even with a national environment that has at times favored Democrats, a challenger with limited resources in a district this red faces a steep path. The seat is rated Safe Republican, with Thompson heavily favored to return to Congress.
